verbalization: Myricetin appears to have a shared target, Alpha-actinin-1, through a chain of interactions involving the Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase. This relationship is supported by two distinct paths, both of which indicate that Myricetin acts as a target for a compound that ultimately targets Alpha-actinin-1. The first path links Myricetin to the Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase via 1-Heptadecene, while the second path connects Myricetin to the same helicase via 2-Carboxy-5-Hydroxy-3-Methoxy-4-Geranylbibenzyl. These two compounds are both potential targets of Myricetin, suggesting a possible mechanism of action where Myricetin may modulate the activity of the Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase, which in turn affects Alpha-actinin-1. The evidence suggests a possible dependency on the helicase activity for the observed effect, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
